tagline: A short county road through the woods, and the odd buffalo.
intro: Blue Ridge Road winds through forest from Newcomb to North Hudson along the southern fringe of the High Peaks, named for Blue Ridge Falls and short on towns. Trails lead off it to the Dix Mountain and Hoffman Notch wildernesses, to the road for Elk Lake and to what is left of the mining village of Tahawus.

Partway along it crosses the Boreas River, where the regional guide says the trout wait for the passing of the sun. Of domesticated animals, the guide adds, buffalo are the only ones a traveler is likely to see. In 1930 the road was made part of Route 73, and around 1936 the state dropped it from the highway system.

moments.title: Tahawus
moments.text: An iron company town given up in 1857 and known after as the deserted village, where Vice President Roosevelt was visiting in 1901 during McKinley's last days.

moments.title: North Hudson
moments.text: The road comes out at North Hudson, a town of 240 at the 2010 census, where a Wild West theme park called Frontier Town ran from 1952 to 1998.
